exposure: prenatal vs. postnatal diagnosis of congenital heart disease
cohort: 111 neonates with prenatal or postnatal diagnosis of congenital heart disease who underwent an emergent intervention within 48 hours postpartum
finding: While 30-day survival did not differ significantly between infants with prenatal and postnatal diagnosis of congenital heart disease, infants with prenatal diagnosis were more likely to be born by cesarean section and those with postnatal diagnosis had a higher need for intubation.
mod_finding: Infants with prenatal diagnosis of congenital heart disease were more likely to be born by caesarean section.
